list: The official 55-trophy PS5 list, frozen 2026-11-18: 1 Platinum, 2 Gold, 6 Silver, 46 Bronze; 28 hidden. All single-player, all offline.
difficulty: PowerPyx rates the Platinum 4/10, about 200 hours.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the Platinum, so there is no separate task to chase: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. Plan around the long tail rather than this trophy itself, because the real work sits in 100% completion, the 250 stunts and the 100 WAiNK locations. PowerPyx rates the whole set 4/10 in difficulty and about 200 hours, so expect a long, steady grind rather than a hard one. Nothing here is online and nothing needs a harder difficulty, since the game has no difficulty settings. Keep your manual saves tidy and finish the missable meditation early, and this trophy takes care of itself. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and the trophy unlocks when it ends. This is the first story trophy most players will earn, and it cannot be missed: just keep following the mission markers until the mission completes. There is no mission replay in the game, but that does not matter here, because the trophy is tied to finishing the mission once. If you are hunting trophies, use this early stretch to learn the controls and the swap between Jason and Lucia. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. Story trophies are unmissable: they unlock automatically as you play through the chapters in order. Chapter 1 is also where the game's one risky trophy lives, so before you finish the chapter, do Lucia's balcony meditation at Jason's house (see Positive Mental Attitude) and make a manual save at the start of the chapter. That single precaution is the most important thing you can do in Chapter 1. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 in full and the trophy unlocks at its close. Like every chapter trophy, it is unmissable and needs nothing beyond playing the story missions in order. Chapter 2 is where Jason and Lucia become playable together, which opens up the partner trophies and the activities that need both of them. Use the chapter to start side content that needs two characters, such as meditating at spots with both of them. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter anyway, since there is no mission replay and no New Game Plus. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its end and the trophy unlocks automatically. There is nothing extra to do and nothing to miss: chapter trophies are awarded for finishing the story missions, not for how you play them. By this point in the story, most of Leonida's map and side activities should be open, so it is a good moment to clear stranger missions and collectibles between story beats. Keep a manual save at the start of each chapter as insurance, because the game offers no mission replay. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4 and the trophy pops at the chapter's close. As with the other chapter trophies, it is unmissable and unlocks simply by completing the story missions in order. You are now near the end of the story, so before the final mission, make a separate manual save: the final mission trophy is the last story beat, and a save here lets you return to free roam cleanly. After the story, free roam continues, so any unfinished side content can still be completed. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission and this Gold trophy unlocks. It is unmissable in the sense that every playthrough reaches the final mission, but there is no mission replay, so make a manual save before you start it. There are no difficulty trophies and no mission medals, so you can play the finale however suits you. Once it is done, the story is over and free roam opens up for the long cleanup toward 100% completion. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run and the trophy unlocks when the mission ends. Named-mission trophies like this one are unmissable: the mission appears in the story in order, and finishing it is all that is required. There are no gold medals for missions, so you do not need to replay it for a rating or a time. Just follow the mission through to its conclusion and move on to the next story beat. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist and the trophy unlocks at the mission's end. This is one of the named-mission trophies, all of which are unmissable and unlock by finishing the mission once. Heist missions tend to be long and multi-stage, so stock up on ammo and armour before you start, and use cover during the shootouts. There is no mission replay, so enjoy the set piece the first time through. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play and the trophy unlocks when it finishes. Like every named-mission trophy, it is unmissable: the mission comes up in the story in order and you only need to finish it once. No special approach is needed and there are no mission medals to chase. Keep playing the story and this one arrives on its own. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners and the trophy unlocks at the end of the mission. It is a named-mission trophy, so it is unmissable and needs only a single completion. Headliners is one of the later story missions, so you will likely have strong weapons and vehicles by the time it appears. There are no difficulty settings and no mission medals, so play it at your own pace. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown and the trophy unlocks when the mission ends. This is another unmissable named-mission trophy: finish the mission once and it is yours. The mission takes place around Vice City International Airport, so expect a lot of open ground and armed opposition. Stock up beforehand and use the airport's cover and vehicles to your advantage. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory and the trophy unlocks at the mission's close. It is an unmissable named-mission trophy that only needs one completion. Late-story missions like this one are usually long, so go in with full health, armour and ammo, and take the shootouts steadily rather than rushing. There is no mission replay, so a manual save before the mission is good insurance. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist, found in the Progress menu, and this Gold trophy unlocks. PowerPyx calls it the hardest trophy in the set, and it is the reason the Platinum takes about 200 hours. The checklist tracks story progress plus side content: PowerPyx and GTABase report it includes meditation spots, vehicle scans, animal studies and challenge completions, with some categories needing only part of the total (for example 15 of the 18 meditation spots). Everything you do before the checklist appears still counts, and nothing on it is missable. Work through it steadily after the story, using the in-game tracker to see what is left. Sources: PowerPyx, GTABase, Exophase.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts and this Silver trophy unlocks. Stunts are the jumps, near misses, drifts and airtime moments the game counts as you drive and ride around Leonida, so the counter climbs naturally if you drive fast and take jumps. To farm it deliberately, find a ramp or a jump you can repeat, use a fast bike or car, and chain airtime and landings. The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so there is no need to do all 250 in one session. Track your total in the Progress menu. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of side activity at least once and the trophy unlocks. The activity types include the game's sports and pastimes such as bowling, fishing, racing, drone racing, arcade games and the shooting range, among others. You do not need to win or finish any of them, only to start and try each kind once. The safest approach is to visit each activity marker on the map as you explore, so you sample them naturally during the story. The exact full list of activity types is still being mapped by public guides, so check the in-game activity menu and your Progress stats to see which kinds you have tried. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge and this Silver trophy unlocks. The range tracks 42 challenges, according to the count PlayStation publishes, and each one needs a gold-medal score, not just a pass. Practice with the weapon each challenge uses, learn the target patterns, and take your time aiming rather than rushing shots. Ammo for the range is separate from free-roam ammo, so you can retry challenges as often as you like without cost. Work through them in batches between story missions so the grind never feels endless. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations around Leonida and the trophy unlocks. Drone races are found at marked locations on the map; you need a win at every one, not just one win overall. Learn each course's turns and gates before racing flat out, and use the drone's boost on the straights. If you lose a race, you can retry it immediately, so keep at it until you win each location. The exact number of locations is not yet fully mapped in public guides, so use the in-game tracker to confirm which locations still need a win. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races and the trophy unlocks. Only distinct races count, so winning the same race twenty times will not do it: you need twenty separate race events across Leonida. Races appear at markers around the map and in different vehicle classes, so try a mix of street, off-road and water races. Pick a vehicle suited to each race, learn the route on a first attempt, then push for the win on the retry. Your win total is tracked in the Progress menu. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge and the trophy unlocks. Fishing challenges are head-to-head contests where you out-fish Cal, so the goal is to land the better catch, not just to catch anything. Learn the fishing controls first in a casual session: cast, wait for the bite, then reel steadily without snapping the line. When you challenge Cal, stay patient and keep your line tension in the safe zone. You can retry the challenge if you lose, so there is no way to miss it. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Play an arcade game through to its end and the trophy unlocks. Arcade cabinets are found in arcades and bars around Leonida; walk up to one and start a game. You only need to complete one game, not to beat a high score or finish every cabinet, so pick the simplest game on offer. If you fail, you can start again right away at no cost. This is one of the quickest trophies in the set and a good early win. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger mission strand, including his final mission, and the trophy unlocks. Stranger missions appear as stranger markers around Leonida; follow Andy's chain from its first mission through to the last. These strands are not missable and stay available in free roam after the story, so there is no rush. If a strand seems to stall, keep playing the story, since later missions often unlock only after certain story beats. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger mission strand, including his final mission, and the trophy unlocks. Kenton's missions are found through stranger markers, and the chain ends with the mission this trophy names. The strand is not missable and remains available in free roam after the story ends. Work through his missions in order as they appear, and check the map for new stranger markers after each story chapter. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger mission strand, including his final mission, and the trophy unlocks. Billy's missions appear as stranger markers around Leonida; follow the chain from the first mission to the last. The strand is not missable and can be completed in free roam after the story. If his next mission does not appear, advance the story a little and check the map again. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger mission strands and this Silver trophy unlocks. Stranger strands are the side-mission chains given by characters like Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, each ending in its own final-mission trophy. You need eight complete strands, so work through every stranger marker you find rather than stopping after one chain. The strands are not missable and stay open in free roam, so this is a post-story cleanup task as much as a story one. Watch for new stranger markers after each chapter, since some strands only appear later. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger mission strand, including his final mission, and the trophy unlocks. Randy's missions appear through stranger markers; follow the chain in order until the final mission is done. The strand is not missable and remains available after the story, so take it at your own pace. Like the other stranger strands, later missions may only unlock after certain story progress, so keep checking the map. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger mission strand, including his final mission, and the trophy unlocks. Tyrone's missions come through stranger markers around Leonida; play the chain from start to finish. The strand is not missable and can be finished in free roam after the story ends. If the next mission is not showing, advance the story and look for the marker again. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida and the trophy unlocks. PowerPyx counts 18 spots across 10 locations, and meditating at a spot with both Jason and Lucia counts twice; track progress in the game under Progress, then Collections, then Exploration, then Meditations. THIS IS THE ONLY POTENTIALLY MISSABLE TROPHY: in Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning, follow her to the balcony at Jason's house and accept the meditation. That moment disappears after Chapter 1, and PowerPyx says it is not yet confirmed whether the trophy strictly needs it, so do it to be safe and keep a manual save from the start of Chapter 1. Note that some lists count 15 spots rather than 18, so the exact full map is not yet fully mapped in public guides: trust the in-game counter, meditate with both characters wherever you can, and finish the last spots once both characters are playable together after Chapter 2. Sources: PowerPyx, GTABase, Output Lag, Exophase.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for and the trophy unlocks. Bret's hunt is a stranger strand: find his marker, take the hunt, then track the animal and take it down. Bring a scoped rifle and approach slowly, since a unique animal is a one-off target and spooking it can waste a long stalk. The exact animal and its location are not yet fully mapped in public guides, so follow Bret's in-game directions and markers rather than any single fan map. The hunt is not missable and can be done in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full sets of collectible cards and this Silver trophy unlocks. Cards are scattered across Leonida and are tracked in the Collections menu, which shows which cards you have and which sets are still incomplete. Pick up every card you pass while exploring, and use the in-game collection tracker to see which sets are closest to finished. The exact card locations are not yet fully mapped in public guides, so rely on the in-game tracker and on exploring every district rather than a single checklist. Cards are not missable and can all be collected in free roam after the story. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app to scan at 100 locations and this Silver trophy unlocks. WAiNK It is the in-game scanning feature: open it at landmarks, vehicles and points of interest around Leonida and the location counts toward the total. Make it a habit to scan everywhere you go, since the 100 locations add up fastest when you scan while travelling rather than in one dedicated sweep. The same scanning also feeds the 100% completion checklist, which asks for 200 vehicle scans out of 277, according to PowerPyx and GTABase. Nothing here is missable, and every location stays available in free roam. Sources: PowerPyx, GTABase, Exophase.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges and the trophy unlocks. Challenges are the game's assorted side goals, tracked in the Progress menu, and they cover driving, combat, exploration and activities. You do not need to complete every challenge in the game, only 50 of them, so pick the easiest ones first and let the harder ones come later. Many challenges complete themselves while you chase other trophies, such as races, stunts and shooting-range medals. PowerPyx and GTABase report the 100% checklist asks for 70 of the 80 challenges, so this trophy is a natural milestone on the way there. Sources: PowerPyx, GTABase, Exophase.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level and then lose it, and the trophy unlocks. The partner must be with you when you escape, so do this during a mission or activity where Jason and Lucia are together, or with a companion in free roam. Raise your wanted level by committing crimes in a busy area, then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the stars to fade. A fast car and a quiet hiding spot, such as an alley or a tunnel, make the escape much easier. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without losing your wanted level, and the trophy unlocks. The trick is the wording: you must keep a wanted level through all three robberies, so do not let the heat fade between shops. Pick three shops close together, plan a fast route between them, and keep moving. Rob each one quickly, get back in the car, and hit the next before the police lose you. If the wanted level drops to zero, the chain breaks and you must start again. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles and the trophy unlocks. Vehicles count as discovered when you find and scan or drive them, and the game tracks how many distinct models you have seen. Explore every district, visit car parks, dealerships and quiet streets, and scan anything new with the WAiNK app as you go. The 100% completion checklist asks for 200 vehicle scans out of 277, according to PowerPyx and GTABase, so this trophy is a milestone on a longer road. Nothing is missable: every vehicle type stays available in free roam. Sources: PowerPyx, GTABase, Exophase.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Defeat five enemies during one use of Combat Focus and the trophy unlocks. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode, so the goal is to line up five takedowns before the effect ends. The easiest setup is a mission or gang shootout where enemies cluster together: trigger Combat Focus when several are in view, aim for the head, and keep moving between targets. A high-capacity weapon helps, since reloading wastes precious focus time. If you only get three or four, retry the same fight until five fall in one use. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in an unscheduled way and the trophy unlocks. The description points to taking off from VCIA without going through the normal departure process, in practice stealing a plane and flying out of the airport. Get onto the airfield, find a plane, and take off before airport security stops you. The exact trigger is not yet fully confirmed in public guides, so expect some trial and error: try a runway takeoff in a stolen aircraft rather than a normal flight. It is not missable and can be attempted any time in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This trophy involves the Rhino tank, as the description hints, but the exact trigger is not yet fully confirmed in public guides, so treat this as a partial guide. The most likely reading is that you need to drive, steal or survive in a Rhino tank, which appears when your wanted level is high or at military locations. Raise your wanted level to draw military attention, then deal with the Rhinos that arrive. Do not rely on a single fan theory: check the in-game stats and updated guides, and try driving a Rhino first, since that is the simplest reading of the description. It is not missable and can be attempted in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected and the trophy unlocks. The key is stealth: enter the store quietly, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, and take the goods without raising an alarm. Go at a quiet time, move slowly, and leave the same way you came in. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting your way out. A manual save before the robbery lets you retry cleanly. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one, and this Silver trophy unlocks. Bank vault robberies are major heist-style jobs: break into the vault, grab the cash, and then escape the police response. Plan each robbery with a fast getaway car parked nearby and a route out of the area before you go in. The five robberies do not need to happen in one session, so take them one at a time between other activities. Losing the wanted level after each robbery is what counts, so do not rush the escape. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape, and the trophy unlocks. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida; spot one on the road, block it or force it to stop, then break into the back and take the cash. The robbery raises your wanted level, so have a getaway car ready and a route planned before you strike. Ram the truck to a stop or use explosives on its rear doors, grab the money quickly, and lose the police. If a truck proves hard to find, cruise the main highways and commercial districts where they run. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Visit every area of Leonida and the trophy unlocks. Exploration is tracked by district: the game counts an area as explored once you have travelled through it, and the Progress menu shows which regions are still unvisited. Drive the highways first to cover the map's skeleton, then sweep through the smaller districts, beaches, swamps and islands. Flying helps for the far corners and the islands. Nothing here is missable, and this trophy pairs naturally with the WAiNK scanning and vehicle discovery grinds. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida and the trophy unlocks. Gangs run hidden operations such as stash houses and drug labs; find one per gang, rob it, and move on to the next gang's territory. The exact number of gangs and the location of each operation are not yet fully mapped in public guides, so use the in-game map and any gang intel you pick up in missions to find them. Operations stay available in free roam, so this is a cleanup task rather than a story one. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy the view, and the trophy unlocks. This is a quiet, atmospheric trophy: head to a beachfront bar on Ocean Drive, buy a drink, and take in the ocean view. It is best done at sunset, which fits the moment the trophy's name is nodding to. There is no combat and no timer, so it is one of the most relaxing trophies in the set. It is not missable and can be done at any point in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight through a showroom's glass front and out onto the street, and the trophy unlocks. Pick a vehicle showroom, get a fast car, and smash through the display windows in the classic style the description hints at. Make sure you are inside the showroom in a vehicle first, then aim for the glass and accelerate through it. Expect a wanted level afterwards, so have an escape route ready. It is not missable and can be done in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and the trophy unlocks. Head to the alley, start a game, and follow through a frame: the trophy is about playing there, not about a perfect score. Bowling is one of the game's social activities and can be played with your partner, which fits the trophy's name. Learn the aim and power controls on your first bowl, then enjoy the game. It is not missable and can be done any time in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description points to a partnership that gains mass appeal, which most likely means building a large following or audience with your partner, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in public guides, so treat this as a partial guide. The likeliest reading is a social-media or fame milestone tied to Jason and Lucia together, so keep doing partner activities and anything that raises your public profile. Do not chase a single fan theory: check the in-game stats for follower or fame counters and updated guides as the community pins the trigger down. It is not listed as missable by any source, so it should be achievable in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, GTA Zone.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices that change your Criminal Profile and the trophy unlocks once you have made enough of them. GTA Zone reports the count as 500 profile-changing actions, though that figure is not yet fully confirmed in public guides, so treat the number as reported rather than certain. Play naturally and make decisions in missions and free roam: the counter climbs as you act, for better or worse. One warning from GTA Zone matters here: do not push your profile toward the Irredeemable rating, because that rating is permanent. Spread your choices and check the Criminal Profile screen to see how your actions are landing. Sources: GTA Zone, Exophase, PSNProfiles.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description, 'Second time's the charm', suggests succeeding at something on a second attempt after failing it once, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in public guides, so treat this as a partial guide. The most plausible reading is that you fail a challenge, race or activity and then pass it on the immediate retry. If that is the trigger, it will likely pop on its own during normal play, since everyone fails a race or a challenge sooner or later. Do not force it by failing deliberately until the community confirms the trigger; just keep playing and watch for it after a retry success. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, GTA Zone.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange out in Leonida and the trophy unlocks. The description points to one of the game's odd, unexplained encounters, the kind of moment players swap stories about, and the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in public guides, so treat this as a partial guide. The likeliest candidates are a UFO sighting or another paranormal event in a remote spot at night, so explore the map's odd corners after dark and keep an eye on the sky. Check updated community guides for the confirmed encounter before making a dedicated trip. It is not missable and should be doable in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, GTA Zone.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by and the trophy unlocks. A melee drive-by means attacking from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon, so equip a bat or similar weapon, get a passenger-side opening, and drive past a pedestrian at low speed while swinging. Pick a quiet street with a lone pedestrian and a slow approach, since a fast pass makes the swing hard to land. The exact conditions are not yet fully confirmed in public guides, so if one clean hit does not pop it, try a slower pass and a direct hit. It is not missable and can be done in free roam. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts and the trophy unlocks. Marked Bills are dirty cash you pick up from robberies and heists, and your contacts can clean them for a cut. Keep laundering after every big job rather than letting the bills pile up, and the total climbs steadily toward $250,000. The counter is cumulative, so it does not need to happen in one laundering session. Check the in-game money and contacts menus to see your laundering total and which contacts are available. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops and the trophy unlocks. The total is cumulative across every shop in the game: clothes, weapons, ammo, food, car parts and anything else you buy. It adds up naturally over a full playthrough, especially once you start buying weapons and vehicle upgrades. If you are close to the total late in the game, spend the remainder on ammo and upgrades you will actually use rather than wasting it. Check your spending in the in-game stats to see how close you are. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in Leonida and the trophy unlocks. Garage properties are bought through the in-game property or real-estate menu, and each one gives you storage for your vehicles. Save up through the story and the robbery trophies, then buy the garages one by one as you can afford them. The exact number of garage properties is not yet fully mapped in public guides, so use the property menu to see which ones you still own. All of them stay available in free roam, so nothing here can be missed. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app and the trophy unlocks. The Scooter Bros app is the in-game delivery and vehicle service: open it, pick a vehicle you own or have found, and register it to the app. Repeat with ten different vehicles, mixing cars, bikes and anything else the app accepts. You do not need ten rare vehicles: ten ordinary ones you find on the street will do. The registration count is tracked in the app itself, so check there to see how many you still need. Sources: Exophase, PSNProfiles, PowerPyx.
